questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Needless to say, cooking (has become) easier now.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'No improvement'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**The given underlined phrase doesn't need any improvement.**

 
• **According to grammar, **the present perfect tense is used to tell when the situation is happened and still continuing in the present.
 
• Let's see the given options-
 
 
• 'has becoming' is incorrect because 'with has we can't write 'becoming' which is -ing form of the verb.'
 
• 'have become' is incorrect because with the singular noun we need to use the singular verb. In the given sentence, the subject is 'cooking' which is singular in number.
 
• So the given phrase doesn't need any improvement.
 
 

**So the correct sentence-** *Needless to say, cooking has become easier now. *

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

The footpath (had been hijacked) by gigantic blue-and-green barricades.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'No improvement'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the usage of** 'had been hijacked' is correct.**
 
• We need a passive voice in the sentence to show that the doer of hijacking is somebody else's. 
 
• Let's see the options-
 
 
• 'have been hijacked' we can't write 'have' with the singular subject because the noun 'footpath' is singular.
 
• 'have being hijacked' we can't write the -ing form of the verb with 'have' hence it is incorrect.
 
• 'Had been hijacking' as it is already stated that we need a passive voice and the structure of the passive voice is 'been +V3' hence this option is also incorrect.
 
 

**So the correct sentence is-** *The footpath had been hijacked by gigantic blue-and-green barricades.*

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

“Do you really come from Spain?” said the Queen.

options.text: The Queen asked did he really came from Spain.
The Queen enquired about his country.
The Queen asked whether he really came from Spain.
The Queen ask which country he is from.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'The Queen asked whether he really came from Spain'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's see the following steps to change the Direct speech to Indirect speech-
 
 
• **Firstly,** see the type of sentence. The given sentence is an imperative sentence and interrogative sentence because the reported speech starts with a verb i.e. 'do' also at the end of the sentence we have a question mark.
 
• **Secondly,** see the tense of the verb the given sentence is in the present tense.
 
• **Thirdly,** if we have a question mark in the sentence then we have to use 'if/whether' in the indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **So after following these steps the correct indirect speech is-** *The Queen asked whether he really came from Spain.*

questions.question:
**Direction- In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the one which best expresses the meaning of the given word.**

Hyperbole
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Overstatement'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The best option that expresses the meaning of the given word** "Hyperbole"** is **option 2, "Overstatement."**
 
• The word** "Hyperbole" **refers to **an exaggerated statement or claim that is not meant to be taken literally, usually used for emphasis or effect**.
 
 
• For example, "He is so hungry that he could eat a horse" is a hyperbole because it exaggerates the degree of hunger to make a point.
 
 
 
• **Overstatement **refers to **the act of exaggerating something beyond its actual significance or importance**. It is a type of **hyperbole **that is used to emphasize a point or to make something appear more impressive or dramatic.
 
 
• Example of overstatement: "I've been waiting for ages." - In this sentence, the speaker is using overstatement to exaggerate the amount of time they've been waiting. They may not have actually been waiting for a very long time, but they want to emphasize their impatience.
 
 
 
• **Option 1, "Spoliation," **refers to the act of plundering or looting, and is not related to the meaning of "Hyperbole."
 
 
• For example, "The invaders engaged in **spoliation **of the city's treasures" means that the invaders looted the city's treasures.
 
 
 
• **Option 3, "Simplification,"** refers to the process of making something simpler or easier to understand, and is not related to the meaning of "Hyperbole."
 
 
• For example, "She **simplified **the instructions for the children to follow" means that she made the instructions easier to understand for the children.
 
 
 
• **Option 4, "Injury," **refers to physical harm or damage caused to a person or object, and is not related to the meaning of "Hyperbole."
 
 
• For example, "He suffered a severe **injury **to his leg in the accident" means that he suffered physical harm to his leg.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is** option 2, "Overstatement," **which accurately expresses the meaning of **"Hyperbole."**

questions.question:
**Directions: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

We wish to make globalization a means to expand human well being and freedom, (1)/ and to bring democracy and developmental (2)/ to local communities where people live. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'3' i.e. error lies in the third part of the sentence**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**In the third part of the sentence,** the usage of **'developmental'** is incorrect Instead, use **'development'**

 
• **According to grammar,** whenever two nouns/verbs/adjectives are connected with the conjunction 'and' then they should be in the same form.
 
• Hence, 'democracy' is the noun and development is a noun too.
 
• 'Developmental' is an adjective that is incorrect.

**So the correct sentence is**- *We wish to make globalization a means to expand human well being and freedom, and to bring **democracy and development **to local communities where people live.*
